content.comment_body: Hello, I need to create a software backup of an older [product_name] model with article number [article_no]. This device has a memory module with article number [article_no]. I plan to use [product_name] software version [version_no] and a USB cable (after removing the memory module, then connecting the USB cable). When I try connecting, I receive an 'Unable to access the IP address Com4' message, even though I selected the correct cable. The USB cable is attached to COM4 according to Windows hardware specs. What is the correct way to back up software from this older device?
It seems there could be an issue with the USB cable or the virtual interface. Is the USB cable an original from [company_name], or a replica from another manufacturer?

The USB cable I'm using is an original from [company_name]. Additionally, communication with newer versions of [product_name] works fine using this USB cable. I am also operating with an original [product_name] laptop from [company_name]. Could the issue be related to the fact that the standard memory module [article_no] is installed in this device?
Have you installed the correct driver for the original [company_name] USB cable?
Yes, I have installed the USB cable driver. Can you explain the purpose of the memory module [article_no] that I need to remove before connecting the USB cable to the device?
The older [product_name] is a first generation device (year 1996). To connect it to a PC, you need to set the device in transfer mode. There are two options for doing this. See attached for details.
Thank you for the advice, the issue is resolved.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced difficulty when attempting to back up software from an older [product_name] device using [product_name] software version [version_no] and an original [company_name] USB cable, receiving a COM port communication error. Troubleshooting involved checking hardware authenticity, driver installation, and requirements for setting the device into transfer mode, highlighting common challenges when interfacing legacy hardware with modern systems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated a simple backup procedure for legacy [product_name] hardware using standard [company_name] software and equipment, without encountering connection issues.
